sample_unit: low-dose chest CT scans (from 6127 screening participants)

links.outcome: Sybil AUC for lung cancer risk by sex subgroup at 1 and 6 years
links.effect: 1-year AUC 0.89 females vs 0.89 males (p=0.92); 6-year AUC 0.87 females vs 0.79 males (p=0.01), better in females.
links.quote: At 6 years, the AUC was 0.87 (95% CI: 0.83-0.93) for females and 0.79 (95% CI: 0.72-0.86) for males, p = 0.01.

links.outcome: Sybil performance on local health-system LDCT data against outcomes
links.effect: Sybil achieved 1-year AUCs of 0.89 in both sexes on 10,573 real-world LDCTs from one health system.
links.quote: In conclusion, Sybil can accurately predict future lung cancer risk in females and males in a real-world setting and performs better in females than in males for predicting 6-year lung cancer risk.

screen.reason: Retrospective external validation study specifically evaluating algorithmic fairness/equity (performance disparity across sex) of an existing deep learning model (Sybil) in a real-world clinical cohort.
